plain: Teams Phone subscriptions include a number of free resource-account licenses you still have to acquire in the admin center.
why: Free does not mean already present.
config: Buy the zero-price SKU and assign it.
fault: Queues are built before any resource-account license exists in the tenant.

plain: The prerequisite article says the tenant needs Teams Phone licensing for the voice-app services to exist.
why: A tenant with only resource accounts and no phone-system license will not behave.
config: Confirm a real Teams Phone license exists.
fault: The first queue is created in an empty tenant and never answers.

plain: A shared Global Administrator account erases the audit of who changed a route.
why: Named accounts, voice roles.
config: Remove shared admin use from the voice runbook.
fault: The SBC password and the global admin password are the same note.

plain: Use 555 numbers and example domains in labs. They are not a customer directory.
why: Find-and-replace onto a real tenant is how labs become incidents.
config: Keep lab names obvious.
fault: A practice script targets production.

plain: A certification you forget to renew expires for you. A retirement means Microsoft withdrew the exam. They are different calendars.
why: MS-700 can lapse in your transcript and still be a live exam for others.
config: Renew on Learn. Check the retirement list separately.
fault: Someone says MS-700 is retired because theirs expired.

plain: Microsoft’s practice questions, when published, match the exam more honestly than a random PDF.
why: AB-250’s page has warned that the practice assessment may lag the live exam.
config: Use it if it exists, and still read the study guide.
fault: A third-party dump is the only study tool.

plain: The half hour you staff, not the daily average divided into imaginary hours.
why: Erlang inputs are interval math.
config: Export that interval.
fault: The link is fine at noon and dead at 09:15.

plain: Whether the agent was in the state the schedule promised. It needs a real state feed from the contact center.
why: Teams presence is a weak substitute for contact-center state.
config: Feed the contact-center state to WFM.
fault: Agents look available in Teams during after-call work.

plain: A pair: a percent and a number of seconds, plus the abandon rule. ‘Eighty twenty’ means nothing until both are defined.
why: Write it down.
config: Use the same definition in the report and in Erlang.
fault: Two dashboards disagree and both claim victory.

plain: The hold file is a copyrighted work unless you made it or licensed it.
why: Uploading a song is not a technical setting.
config: Use a track you can defend.
fault: A famous song plays to every caller.

plain: The people the emergency policy emails or messages when an emergency call starts.
why: An empty group is a silent policy.
config: Put facilities or security in it and test.
fault: Responders arrive and nobody inside knows which floor.

plain: A location specific enough for a responder to find the caller. A city name is not enough for a campus.
why: Floors and suites matter.
config: Validate the civic detail you can defend.
fault: The PSAP receives only the city.

plain: The number or process the carrier gave you for emergency tests. It is not the public emergency number.
why: Curiosity calls to the real service are how you meet the police and a fine.
config: Use the test process and write down the result.
fault: A lab dials the real emergency number.

plain: VPN configuration that sends only corporate apps through the tunnel and lets Teams media go direct.
why: Full tunnel is the opposite.
config: Test a call both ways.
fault: Media stays in the tunnel and RTT doubles.

plain: A switch copy of packets so you can see DSCP at the egress without standing on the user’s keyboard.
why: The proof of QoS lives there.
config: Mirror the egress and filter the audio ports.
fault: QoS is declared done from a screenshot of a policy object.

plain: A router rule that sets DSCP based on the port range, useful for devices that will not mark for themselves.
why: Combine it with client marks where you can.
config: Match 50000–50059 and the signaling range you cannot move.
fault: The ACL matches a range from an old design guide.

plain: A call has media each way. Sizing one direction and forgetting the other undersizes a symmetric policer.
why: State which number you quoted.
config: Multiply by concurrent calls and say per direction.
fault: The policer is symmetric and the plan was one way only.

plain: G.722 at 160 bytes every 20 ms pays the same header tax as G.711. Wideband does not remove IP headers.
why: Do not quote 64 kbit/s as the link budget.
config: Use the same 80 and 87.2 figures when the payload size matches.
fault: A wideband design is sized at 64 kbit/s.

plain: Silence suppression lowers the average and not the peak. Size the peak.
why: A quiet average hides an all-hands call.
config: Use the busy codec rate.
fault: The link was sized for silence.

plain: A quiet week on the new path before you delete the old trunk.
why: Friday-night deletion is not a cleanup task.
config: Calendar the deletion separately from the cut.
fault: The old trunk is removed in the same change window.

plain: Move people who call each other in the same migration wave so they do not trombone for a year.
why: Tromboning is a cost.
config: Group the move by community.
fault: Every call between a moved user and a stayed user hairpins all year.

plain: Contact-center numbers stay on UCCE. User numbers go to Teams. The SBC enforces the split.
why: One route pattern that sends everything to Teams strands the IVR.
config: List the ranges.
fault: The IVR DN is sent to a Teams user who does not exist.

plain: Supervisor features such as whisper and barge belong to the contact-center product, not to a Teams peer call.
why: Do not promise them from a Teams calling policy.
config: Read the CCaaS guide.
fault: Supervisors expect Teams to whisper on a Calling Plan user.

plain: If the contact center and Teams both record, you still need one Call-ID to know it is the same conversation.
why: Two audio files without a key are two rumors.
config: Store the key in both systems.
fault: Compliance cannot find the file that matches the case.

plain: Recording, desktop capture, and directory search all need a privacy decision before go-live.
why: A surprise recorder fails the review in public.
config: Write what is captured and who can play it.
fault: A desktop recorder is discovered by the privacy team after launch.

plain: A retention setting you have never restored is a hope. Ask the recording partner for one file back.
why: Legal hold on a mailbox does not do this.
config: Restore a test call.
fault: A regulator asks and the bucket policy already deleted the audio.

plain: Quality scores should use a form published to the people being scored.
why: Secret criteria are not coaching.
config: Publish the form first.
fault: Agents are coached on a form they have never seen.

plain: Queue totals have to be able to leave the contact center on a schedule the WFM tool can read.
why: A screenshot is not a feed.
config: Automate the interval export.
fault: Staffing is retyped from a dashboard every Monday.

plain: If shrinkage is a guess, say it is a guess. Thirty percent is not a law of nature.
why: Hidden assumptions become fights.
config: Print the assumption on the staffing sheet.
fault: The roster is tight because shrinkage was silently zero.

plain: High occupancy next to rising abandons means the service level is being spent to look efficient.
why: Watch both.
config: Put occupancy beside service level.
fault: A site celebrates 95 percent occupancy while callers hang up.

plain: E.164, Call-ID, queue, agent. Four fields make a case auditable.
why: A free-text note does not.
config: Make the pop write them.
fault: The case says ‘called customer’ and the recording cannot be found.

plain: A list of utterances whose correct intent you already know. Run it before you publish a prompt change.
why: Foundry is a place to do this. A phone number is not.
config: Keep the set in the project.
fault: Friday’s prompt change has no test utterances.

plain: A design that needs a product Microsoft has not shipped is not a hook. It is a bet.
why: Hooks in this campus use today’s policies, events, and identifiers.
config: Delete the rumor from the design.
fault: Go-live depends on a feature from a keynote that is not in the docs.

plain: The Direct Routing page that shows whether Teams considers the SBC healthy.
why: It reflects OPTIONS and pairing, not your feelings about the carrier.
config: Read it beside the SBC log.
fault: The page says unhealthy and the dial plan is edited anyway.

plain: Inbound and outbound are different routes. A successful outbound call does not prove the carrier can deliver inbound.
why: Always do both.
config: Place one of each and keep the Call-IDs.
fault: Outbound works and the published number is silent.

plain: You care that the emergency call leaves, and that the location and notification are correct. Inbound to the queue is a different test.
why: Do not mix the evidence.
config: Use the carrier test process.
fault: A normal inbound call is filed as the emergency test.

plain: Two dates that take companies down: the holiday the attendant does not know, and the certificate that expires.
why: Put both on one calendar.
config: Review them quarterly.
fault: The office is closed and the certificate expires the same weekend.

plain: Contoso, Fabrikam, and 555 numbers in this campus are samples. They are not your tenant.
why: Do not whois them and open a ticket.
config: Use them only as shapes for a design.
fault: A runbook still says contoso.com in production.

plain: 14 October 2026 is when this campus was compared with Learn. It is not a promise the page stays still.
why: Say the date when you quote a retirement.
config: Re-open Learn before you book or you change production.
fault: A 2024 screenshot is treated as current.

plain: Microsoft’s QoS article recommends DSCP 46 (EF, Expedited Forwarding) for Teams audio, with initial client source ports 50000–50019.
why: A mark only helps if every hop agrees. Audio waiting in the default queue is how words drop out.
config: Enable QoS markers in the Teams admin center and match the port range on the network. Signaling ports are not configurable.
fault: Audio packets in the documented port range arrive at the WAN edge marked 0.

plain: The recommended initial client source ports for audio are 50000–50019. Browser joins do not use these fixed ranges.
why: Port-based ACLs are how routers mark traffic from devices that cannot set DSCP themselves.
config: Keep the ranges adjacent and non-overlapping if you resize them. Do not resize the signaling range.
fault: An ACL matches the wrong range, so video is queued as audio or as best effort.
